what_it_is.prose: No. 1 Base Repair Depot (1 BRD) at Chakeri, Kanpur is the Indian Air Force's principal overhaul and repair depot for the An-32 medium-transport fleet, operating under Maintenance Command. Formed on 9 August 1948 (from the merger of No. 1 Aircraft Repair Depot and No. 10 Aircraft Storage unit), it has serviced a long line of IAF types — Spitfire, Vampire, Toofani, Mystere, Hunter and Avro/HS-748 — and presently focuses on the Antonov An-32. Under the roughly $400 million An-32RE upgrade contract signed with Antonov of Ukraine in 2009, about 40 aircraft were upgraded in Ukraine and a further ~64 at No. 1 BRD Kanpur under transfer of technology; the first Kanpur-upgraded RE aircraft entered service around 2011. After the RE programme stalled with the Russia-Ukraine war disrupting Ukrainian OEM support, No. 1 BRD became the hub of India's indigenous route — structural overhaul, AI-20 engine overhaul, indigenised spares (the IAF has reported significant cost savings from indigenising An-32 spares) and digital avionics/GPS — increasingly in partnership with private Indian firms, as the IAF drew up a roadmap to overhaul around 60 An-32 to keep the fleet flying toward 2040. It uniquely retains its original motto 'SAHAYATA SEVA'.

faq.question: What does No. 1 BRD Kanpur do?
faq.answer: No. 1 Base Repair Depot at Chakeri, Kanpur is the IAF's overhaul and repair depot for the An-32 medium-transport fleet, under Maintenance Command. Formed in 1948, it has serviced many IAF types over its history and today focuses on the An-32, including the transfer-of-technology upgrade of ~64 aircraft to RE standard and the current indigenous overhaul and life-extension effort.

faq.question: What is No. 1 BRD's role in keeping the An-32 flying after the Russia-Ukraine war?
faq.answer: With Antonov (Ukraine) OEM support disrupted, No. 1 BRD became the hub of India's indigenous An-32 route — structural overhaul, AI-20 engine overhaul, indigenised spares (the IAF reported around ₹160 crore saved) and digital avionics — increasingly with private Indian firms, under a roadmap to overhaul about 60 airframes toward 2040.
